result.title: MESSI: Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration for Physics-Based Character Control
result.summary: Physics-based soccer characters must perform diverse motor skills and transition smoothly between them, such as dribbling into a shot. However, skills that perform well in isolation may fail when executed sequentially, as preceding behaviors can leave the character and ball in unfamiliar states. We present MESSI (Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration), a framework that enables multiple soccer skill transitions through shared adaptation while preserving the original skill policy outside transitions. MESSI first trains eight task-competent experts using motion priors and task rewards, then distills them into a unified, skill-conditioned Transformer. Rather than retraining individual experts for different transitions, we train a shared, context-conditioned low-rank adapter on the frozen student through online reinforcement learning. Activated upon skill switching, the adapter helps the target skill handle unfamiliar entry states, while a learned exit mechanism determines when to return control to the original student. By disabling the adapter during native skill execution, MESSI preserves the original student policy by construction. Experiments across individual skills, skill transitions, and continuous skill chains demonstrate substantial improvements over direct switching, including an increase in dribbling-to-shooting success from 19.8% to 61.8%.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作面向物理仿真足球角色控制，先把八个技能专家蒸馏为统一的技能条件 Transformer，再在冻结学生策略上训练共享的低秩适配器，仅在技能切换时激活以应对陌生进入状态，并由学习到的退出机制决定何时交还控制权。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「切换时临时启用适配器、由学习到的退出机制关闭、以构造方式保留原策略」可供核查作为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的模式门控与停止决策类比，可能启发在进入姿态异常时短程修正而不损伤基础推理能力。
